intended_object: The canonical base-change isomorphism S ⊗_R (R[x]/I_R)_d ≅ (S[x]/I_S)_d of S-modules. Here I is the Hankel ideal of the rational normal curve, and (–)_d is the degree-d homogeneous component of the quotient. The docstring and module docs describe it as sending s ⊗ b_i to s • b_i, compatibly with the full-quotient scalar-change equivalence.
explanation:
The library already has a basis of the degree-d component, indexed by Fin (n*d+1), and the same index set is used over every base ring. The definition takes the base change of the R-basis, which is an S-basis of S ⊗_R H(R,n,d), and matches it index by index with the basis of H(S,n,d). The two bases correspond under the identity on the index set, so this linear equivalence sends s ⊗ b_i to s • b_i.

The theorem `quotientHomogeneousBaseChangeEquiv_coe` proves that the map is the right one. Composed with the inclusion into the full quotient, it equals the canonical map: base change of the inclusion, followed by the full-quotient algebra equivalence `quotientBaseChangeAlgEquiv`. So this is the natural isomorphism, not an arbitrary one. The library's audit test also checks the case ℤ → ZMod 2.

R and S are arbitrary commutative rings and n, d are arbitrary. The object is specific to the Hankel/rational normal curve quotient, which is its intended setting, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has the generic tools used here (`Module.Basis.baseChange`, `Module.Basis.equiv`) but no specific counterpart for this object.
